newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy seen aiming for deficit/GDP of 2.8% in '98.
newsitem.headline: Italy seen aiming for deficit/GDP of 2.8% in '98.

text.p: The Italian government is likely to lower its 1998 target for the ratio between budget deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) to 2.8 percent from the current 3.0 percent goal, newspapers reported on Friday.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi later on Friday is expected to present the centre-left cabinet with the outlines of the government's programme of three-year economic forecasts (DPEF) for the period 1998-2000.

European Union finance ministers, in a strongly worded document released earlier this week, urged Italy to aim for a deficit/GDP ratio below the three percent threshold established in the Maastricht Treaty for EMU aspirants.
Left-leaning L'Unita newspaper, which has close ties to the govenrnment, said the Treasury was preparing a 1998 budget which would include 27 trillion lire of deficit cuts.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the package might be worth up to 29 trillion lire, while Corriere della Sera daily said the budget would seek somewhere between 25-27 trillion lire of cuts.

L'Unita said the government was hoping to save up to eight trillion lire next year off its the welfare bill, with a further four trillion lire coming from a block on early retirements in the teaching sector.

In all, the government wanted to raise 10 trillion lire next year in additional revenues, with six trillion lire of this coming from a revision of value added tax (VAT) bands which is necessary under European Union directives.
The rest of the money will come from clamping down on public administration spending and transfers to state bodies such as the railways, L'Unita said.

Il Sole 24 Ore and L'Unita said the government would set a new GDP target of two percent for next year against the exisiting 2.8 percent official forecast, while the inflation goal would remain pegged to two percent. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
